source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Florence, Kentucky campus publishes 5 MW of IT capacity, the largest published megawatt figure of any mapped facility in Kentucky.

The state has five mapped facilities, but only three publish a megawatt figure, totaling 9.55 MW. That means the ranking is partly a statement about disclosure. A facility that publishes nothing cannot be compared, and most mapped sites in Kentucky publish nothing. The 5 MW figure is small against the hundreds of megawatts at the largest AI campuses, so its significance is local: it is the only large number the state currently puts on the record.

The building also publishes 143,000 square feet of technical space, but no rack count, no accelerator count, and no power density. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 5 MW supports roughly 125 racks. At 10 kW per rack it supports about 500. The published figure alone does not say which the building was designed for, so any conversion to racks or chips is an outside estimate, not the operator's.

The certifications, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II, and Green Globes, qualify the campus for regulated workloads. They do not establish that any particular tenant is present, and no tenant list is published. What the data does not cover is equally important: no expansion plans, no power purchase arrangements, no interconnection status, and no indication of what the site's 5 MW is actually used for.
